'''Manhattanville''' (also known as '''West Harlem''' or '''West Central Harlem''', after its location near [[Harlem]]) is a neighborhood in the [[New York City]] [[Boroughs of New York City|borough]] of [[Manhattan]]. It is bordered on the north by [[135th Street (Manhattan)|135th Street]]; on the south by 122nd and [[125th Street (Manhattan)|125th Street]]s; on the west by [[Hudson River]]; and on the east by [[Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard]] and the campus of [[City College of New York|City College]].<ref name=nyt-westcentralharlem>{{cite news | title = If You're Thinking of Living In/West Central Harlem; Abandonment Down, Refurbishment Up | first= Maggie | last= Garb | work = [[The New York Times]] | date= June 21, 1998 | url = http://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/21/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-west-central-harlem-abandonment-down-refurbishment-up.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150527083125/http://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/21/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-west-central-harlem-abandonment-down-refurbishment-up.html | archive-date=May 27, 2015 | url-status=dead | access-date=December 19, 2025 | quote = The area [West Central Harlem], a slice of 19th-century brownstones, prewar walk-ups and small elevator buildings bounded by 122nd and 134th Streets, Morningside Park and Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard, appears on city maps as the western part of Central Harlem. Some residents call it Manhattanville, the name of the post office on 125th Street near the boulevard.}}</ref><ref name="pesce">{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/life-style/real-estate/guide-west-harlem-manhattanville-neighborhood-article-1.190614|title=A Guide to West Harlem's Manhattanville Neighborhood|last=Pesce|first=Nicole Lyn|date=October 17, 2010|work=[[New York Daily News]]|quote=Whether you call it West Harlem or Manhattanville, the upper-upper West Side is enjoying a second renaissance.| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161025235352/http://www.nydailynews.com/life-style/real-estate/guide-west-harlem-manhattanville-neighborhood-article-1.190614 | archive-date=October 25, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Throughout the nineteenth century, Manhattanville bustled around a wharf active with ferry and daily river conveyances. It was the first station on the [[Hudson River Railroad]] running north from the city, and the hub of daily stage coach, omnibus and streetcar lines. Situated near [[Broadway (Manhattan)|Bloomingdale Road]], its hotels, houses of entertainment and post office made it an alluring destination of suburban retreat from the city, yet its direct proximity to the Hudson River also made it an invaluable industrial entry point for construction materials and other freight bound for [[Upper Manhattan]]. With the construction of road and railway viaducts over the valley in which the town sat, Manhattanville, increasingly absorbed into the growing city, became a marginalized industrial area. In the early 2000s, the neighborhood became the site of a major planned expansion of [[Columbia University]], which has campuses in [[Morningside Heights, Manhattan|Morningside Heights]] to the south and [[Washington Heights, Manhattan|Washington Heights]] to the north.

Manhattanville is part of [[Manhattan Community Board 9|Manhattan Community District 9]], and its primary [[ZIP Code]]s are 10027 and 10031.<ref name="NYCPlanning"/> It is patrolled by the 26th Precinct of the [[New York City Police Department]].
